anabaptist.1: Dordrecht V: only "the unbelieving and disobedient" exclude themselves "through their own sins," implying genuine human response, not monergistic necessity
anabaptist.2: Dordrecht IV: Christ "tasted death and shed His precious blood for all men"; V: "all men without distinction" may become His children through faith
anabaptist.3: Dordrecht V-VI tie salvation to continued faith, obedience, repentance; no "secure in my worst seasons" doctrine; closest to conditional perseverance
anabaptist.4: Dordrecht IV: cause of eternal salvation "for all those who... believe in, and obey Him"
anabaptist.5: Dordrecht V: the disobedient "make themselves unworthy of eternal life" through their own sins — grace enables, response is genuinely free
anabaptist.6: Confessions never ground election in foreseen faith; category absent
anabaptist.7: Supralapsarian order of decrees is foreign scholasticism; confessions silent
anabaptist.8: Dordrecht VI: "through which faith we obtain forgiveness of sins, are sanctified, justified... as being born again" — faith precedes/accompanies new birth, not caused by prior regeneration
anabaptist.9: Dordrecht V: the unbelieving "incur this through their own sins, thus making themselves unworthy" — grace is resistible
anabaptist.10: Dordrecht V excludes from salvation only those who "make themselves unworthy through their own sins" — contradicts decreed reprobation of all things
anabaptist.11: Dordrecht V: the disobedient exclude themselves; XVI: the one who sins unto death is "separated from God, and forfeiting the kingdom of God"
anabaptist.12: Implied by Dordrecht V (see q9): those who make themselves unworthy have resisted God's call
anabaptist.13: Science-vs-Scripture conflict is a modern frame; confessions never address science
anabaptist.14: Dordrecht V: Scripture contains "the whole counsel and will of His heavenly Father"; "neither angel nor man may alter it"; I affirms creation in six days — high, unqualified trust in what it affirms
anabaptist.15: "Saving message vs error-free details" distinction is modernist-era and foreign to the documents
anabaptist.16: Confessions never discuss science or the human authors' cultural limitations
anabaptist.17: Confessions never theorize the inspiration process/mechanism
anabaptist.18: 1978 statement is anachronistic to both confessions
anabaptist.19: "God speaks through it vs theory of writing" contrast is foreign to the documents
anabaptist.21: Confessions cite Jesus authoritatively but never argue from his view of the OT to complete truthfulness as an apologetic thesis
anabaptist.22: Accommodation theory is foreign to the documents
anabaptist.23: Schleitheim I: baptism for "all those who with such an understanding themselves desire and request it from us"
anabaptist.24: Schleitheim I: "hereby is excluded all infant baptism, the greatest and first abomination of the pope"; Dordrecht VII requires penitent believers
anabaptist.25: Schleitheim I (see q24); Dordrecht VII: baptism only of "penitent believers" upon "Scriptural confession of faith"
anabaptist.26: The circumcision-continuity rationale for infant baptism is precisely the paedobaptist argument Schleitheim I and Dordrecht VII reject
anabaptist.27: Schleitheim I: infant baptism excluded; Dordrecht VII: only penitent believers baptized — rebaptism of those baptized as infants is the Anabaptist practice
anabaptist.28: Schleitheim III and Dordrecht X restrict the Supper to those united with Christ by (believer's) baptism; infant communion rejected with infant baptism
anabaptist.29: Neither confession specifies mode; Dordrecht VII says only "baptized with water"
anabaptist.30: Schleitheim I requires repentance, amendment of life, true belief, and personal request — implying a mature profession; no explicit "delay" counsel, hence 1 not 2
anabaptist.31: Confessions affirm the Spirit's gifts for strength/comfort (Schleitheim preface) but are silent on whether miracles/healing/prophecy continue today
anabaptist.32: Tongues never mentioned in either confession
anabaptist.33: Confessions never address specific prophetic words for others
anabaptist.34: Dordrecht IX treats the apostles as past foundation-layers; the church now has teachers, pastors, deacons, deaconesses
anabaptist.35: "Initial evidence" doctrine is Pentecostal and foreign; confessions silent on tongues entirely
anabaptist.36: Confessions never command or discuss seeking/practicing healing and prophecy
anabaptist.37: 1 Cor 13:10 exegesis is absent from the confessions
anabaptist.38: Two-stage Spirit-baptism terminology is foreign; Dordrecht VII ties water baptism to the "renewing of the Holy Ghost" without a distinct second experience
anabaptist.39: Confessions never teach an expectation of healing in response to prayer
anabaptist.40: No millennium in the confessions; Dordrecht XVIII teaches only general resurrection and last judgment
anabaptist.41: Dordrecht IV: Christ sits at God's right hand "whence He will come again to judge"; confessions never frame "already reigning now" as an eschatological system
anabaptist.42: Confessions never address a distinct divine plan for the Jewish people
anabaptist.43: Pretribulational rapture is unknown to the documents; Dordrecht XVIII teaches one general resurrection and judgment
anabaptist.44: Israel-church relation is never addressed (Dordrecht IX's "one flock" of Jews and Gentiles is about unity, not a covenantal schema)
anabaptist.47: Confessions expect a separated, persecuted church (Schleitheim IV), not world Christianization
anabaptist.48: Modern Middle East is anachronistic to both confessions
anabaptist.49: Schleitheim VI: the sword was established "in the law" but is outside "the perfection of Christ"; VII: Christ's perfection forbids what the law commanded (oaths) — different rules across the covenants
anabaptist.50: Dordrecht III: the pious patriarchs "through faith, looked forward" to Christ; IV: the Lamb "foreordained... before the foundation of the world"
anabaptist.51: "Two groups in God's plan" is a dispensational schema the confessions never use
anabaptist.52: Schleitheim VII: Christ, "who teaches the perfection of the law," forbids what the law commanded; Dordrecht V: "the Law of Christ, i.e., the Holy Gospel or the New Testament"
anabaptist.53: Confessions never affirm the Decalogue as a distinct standing moral law; obedience is framed as the Law of Christ (Dordrecht V)
anabaptist.54: Confessions never date the church's origin or contrast Pentecost with Israel
anabaptist.55: "Covenant of works / covenant of grace" framework is Reformed scholasticism, never used by these confessions
anabaptist.56: Literal-vs-spiritual hermeneutic of Israel's prophecies is foreign to the documents
anabaptist.57: Confessions never theorize about NT authors' use of the OT vs original authorial intent
anabaptist.58: Confessions are silent on creative innovation in worship; their simplicity ethic comes from separation (Schleitheim IV), not a stated worship principle
anabaptist.59: See q58 — no position on creativity in worship
anabaptist.62: Schleitheim's Congregational Order says "The Psalter shall be read daily at home" — reading, not exclusive psalmody in worship; no exclusive-psalmody rule
anabaptist.63: Cultural adaptation of worship style never addressed
anabaptist.65: Schleitheim V: the shepherd's office is to "read and exhort and teach"; Congregational Order centers meetings on teaching, reading, prayer, and the Supper
anabaptist.66: "Answers to no one but God" is too absolute: Schleitheim itself was an inter-congregational union, and Dordrecht was adopted by a 51-minister conference "to which all parties should adhere"
anabaptist.67: Conferences exercise mutual, moral accountability (Dordrecht intro), not hierarchical authority "beyond their walls" in the question's sense; no clear position
anabaptist.68: Schleitheim V: "the congregation which has chosen him"; Dordrecht IX: officers "chosen and ordained thereto by the church"
anabaptist.69: Schleitheim V, Dordrecht IX (see q68) — election is by the congregation, not appointment by leaders
anabaptist.70: Schleitheim V: shepherd per "the rule of Paul," not apostolic succession; Dordrecht IX likewise
anabaptist.71: Confessions are ambiguous: Schleitheim V assumes "the shepherd" per congregation; Dordrecht IX uses plural "elders"/"bishops, pastors, and leaders" per city — no clear preference for team vs single le
anabaptist.72: Both confessions were produced by inter-congregational conferences of self-governing churches (Schleitheim union; Dordrecht 1632 conference)
anabaptist.73: Schleitheim III: "in remembrance of the broken body of Christ... shed blood"; Dordrecht X: "in remembrance of the suffering and death of the Lord"
anabaptist.74: Confessions frame the Supper as remembrance and fellowship/unity (Schleitheim III; Dordrecht X: "the unity and fellowship which we have with God and one another") — not a special sacramental presence
anabaptist.75: Dordrecht VII: baptism is "to the burying of their sins" and incorporation "into the communion of the saints" — substantive, not "mostly a public way of showing"
anabaptist.76: Dordrecht VI: "neither baptism, supper, church [membership], nor any other outward ceremony, can without faith, regeneration, change or renewing of life, avail anything" — grace comes through faith, n
anabaptist.77: Schleitheim III, Dordrecht X (see q74) — memorialist
anabaptist.78: Schleitheim Congregational Order: "The Lord's Supper shall be held, as often as the brothers are together" — i.e., at least as often as weekly
anabaptist.79: Lutheran "in, with, and under" rejected; Schleitheim III, Dordrecht X teach remembrance
anabaptist.80: Circumcision-baptism continuity rejected (see q26); Dordrecht VII, Schleitheim I
anabaptist.81: Dordrecht VI: outward ceremony "can without faith... avail nothing" — faith/regeneration, not baptism, is the operative necessity; but baptism is commanded of penitent believers (VII), so -1 not -2
anabaptist.82: Dordrecht VI: "put off the old man with his deeds, and put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness" — real liberation from sin's control
anabaptist.83: Ambiguous: confessions expect real holiness (Dordrecht VI) AND ongoing diligence against falling (Dordrecht XVIII: "use all diligence") — "fighting against sin" conflates vigilance with bondage
anabaptist.84: Confessions hold both a decisive "first lesson" of repentance (Dordrecht VI) and ongoing diligence — the either/or is foreign
anabaptist.85: Confessions expect genuine holiness but never explicitly affirm sinless perfection; the ban articles presuppose believers can fall
anabaptist.86: Wesley's doctrine postdates and is foreign to the confessions
anabaptist.87: "Remain sinners" as Christian identity is absent; confessions describe the new man in righteousness (VI) while practicing discipline for the fallen (XVI)
anabaptist.88: Dordrecht VI (see q82); Schleitheim II expects believers to "walk in His commandments"
anabaptist.89: "Baptism in the Holy Spirit" empowerment terminology is foreign to the confessions
anabaptist.90: Confessions never address women as senior pastors
anabaptist.92: Dordrecht XII frames marriage as two free believing persons in the original order; male headship is not explicitly taught
anabaptist.93: "Equally called to all forms of ministry" never addressed; Dordrecht IX ordains deaconesses but not women teachers
anabaptist.94: Confessions never address the 1 Cor 14 silence passages
anabaptist.95: Complementarianism as a named system is modern and foreign
anabaptist.96: Culture-vs-Scripture framing of gender restrictions is foreign to the documents
anabaptist.97: Dordrecht VI: "bring forth genuine fruits of repentance... eschew evil and do good"; Schleitheim II disciplines those who fail to walk in the commandments
anabaptist.98: Schleitheim II, Dordrecht VI (see q97) — unamended life contradicts the faith confessed
anabaptist.99: Schleitheim II: the ban for those who "slip and fall into error and sin"; Dordrecht XVI: separation of the one who "sins again unto death"
anabaptist.100: Dordrecht VI: "the first lesson of the precious New Testament... is repentance and reformation of life"
anabaptist.101: Dordrecht IV: salvation "for all those who... believe in, and obey Him"; V: "as obedient children, heed, follow, and practice"
anabaptist.102: Dordrecht V-VI tie standing before God to faith joined with obedience and reformation of life — assurance divorced from obedience is foreign
anabaptist.103: Free-grace separation of faith from repentance/obedience directly contradicts Dordrecht VI (see q100)
anabaptist.105: Dordrecht V: the unbelieving and disobedient exclude themselves "through their own sins"; XVI: the sinner "forfeiting the kingdom of God"
